author: @danieldalton6544
komentar: Spoiler Alert: my review. Ok, I just watched it. I was going  WTH throughout. I don’t quite get it. VERY vague and confusing. Too metaphorical and subconscious to the point of triviality. Quite bizarre. The director wrote it after his friend died and each character was a symbol of the 5 stages of grief? But, it withholds key pieces of information. Weapons meaning children are being weaponized by social media? Bad parenting? It was so slow and weird but not knowing why, the rules, the meaning, the point was frustrating as I sat there watching things happen without explanation. Nothing was scary, just weird. None of the characters were likable except maybe the principal and his partner or Alex’s parents before Gladys’ arrival. Why did just one vomit black bile while attacking? How did the kids know to go after Gladys? How’d they have superhuman strength and get not even a scratch jumping through windows and doors? Some plot holes for sure. Why the weird makeup? She looked like a clown which doesn’t exactly help her blend in. I had zero sympathy for Matthew the bully and wanted to punch him in the face. I hoped HE never talked again. This is a lot like Get Out where you don’t know how things are happening (a spoon tapping a tea cup is magic how?) because they don’t explain anything. That approach is supposed to be suspenseful? You’re just watching bizarre, strange things happen and that somehow translates to something profound, scary, or even good? Seemed like a mess to me. A prequel could  go a long way in making this make more sense. Would not recommend or watch again. Sorry, but it just didn’t do it for me just like Get Out. Felt the same about Barbarian so, this is not a writer/director for me. I see why Jordan Peele was so upset he fired his manager because he lost the bidding war because this is right up his alley. 2025, with this and Sinners, the year of the very ambiguous thriller. It can be more scary to not know who the evil person is, or where they’re coming from or what they’re about if it’s grounded in reality but, when you introduce supernatural elements you have to explain something or suspension of disbelief gets strained to the breaking point.

Trailers should reveal a snapshot of the story. They can't give everything away because it's just a trailer. Even then, watching the movie is also about the journey, the emotions and characters and such. Otherwise, you could just stick with the Wikipedia summary, if all you care about is what happens.

That being said, I'm not complaining about this trailer. I do think this trailer was done well. It wasn't just a bunch of out of chaotic scenes with no plot details. There was a plot revealed, but we weren't told why what was happening was happening. I think that works well because the characters don't know why that's all happening either. So if we were to watch the movie, we'd get to figure it out along with the characters.
